name: mcpd-code
instructions:
File and shell tools for coding agents.

- Prefer Grep and Glob over shelling out to `grep` or `find`; they are faster and respect ignore files.
- Prefer Edit over Write for an existing file. Write replaces the whole file.
- Each Bash call runs in its own process, so `cd` and exported variables do not carry over.

tool.name: Bash
tool.description: Executes a given bash command and returns its output. Each call runs in its own process, so nothing persists between calls; prefer absolute paths.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in 5-10 words, in active voice.

tool.name: Read
tool.description: Reads a file from the local filesystem. `file_path` must be an absolute path. Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from.

limit.description: The number of lines to read.

argv: NR >= s && NR < s + n { printf "%6d\t%s\n", NR, $0 }

tool.name: Write
tool.description: Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write.

content.description: The content to write to the file.

tool.name: Edit
tool.description: Performs exact string replacement in a file. `old_string` must match the file exactly and appear exactly once; strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching. After an earlier edit to the same file, match the edited content rather than what you first read.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify.

old_string.description: The text to replace. Must match the file exactly, including indentation.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with. Must differ from old_string.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring exactly one.

tool.name: Glob
tool.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against.

tool.name: Grep
tool.description: Content search built on ripgrep. Full regex syntax — ripgrep, not grep, so escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`). Filter with `glob`, widen with `-C`.

pattern.description: The regular expression to search for.

path.description: File or directory to search in.

glob.description: Glob limiting which files are searched, such as "*.rs".

-C.description: Lines of context to show before and after each match.
